faq: What does this tool calculate?
The intersection of two working days in different time zones — the shared hours, rendered in UTC and in both local times, for a chosen date.
Do I need an account?
No — places and hours in, overlap out.
Can I use the result for professional work?
Yes — rota design, hiring plans and client commitments all start from exactly this computation, done with DST rules rather than static offsets.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — the places are chosen; nothing locates you.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Zone resolutions follow the tz database and open geocoding; the overlap arithmetic itself is exact once zones are set.
Non-9-to-5 hours?
Enter the actual hours — shift work and part-time patterns are first-class inputs, and overlaps follow them faithfully.
Zero overlap — now what?
The honest zero redirects the design: async hand-offs, rotating meeting pain, or one side flexing hours. The calculator shows how much flex buys how much overlap.
Weekends differ by country.
Working weeks vary (Friday–Saturday weekends exist). Model the actual days when the calculator's date framing allows, and sanity-check the human calendar too.
Three locations?
Pairwise overlaps compose: compute A∩B, then intersect with C's window manually — or let the Meeting Time Planner hold the group's clocks at once.
Lunch breaks?
The calculator intersects stated working spans; carve lunches by splitting the day into two spans and intersecting each — the honest arithmetic of real calendars.
Ramadan and seasonal hours?
Real teams flex hours seasonally — enter the season's actual spans and the overlap follows. Courtesy, computed.
